instruction: I went on a trip with friends to Athens recently. I have maintained a note of money I owe to others and others owe me from the trip in simple note. Make private venmo payments or requests accordingly. In the payments/requests, add a note, "For Athens trip".
notes: The note is found via simple_note.search_notes(query='Athens') and read via show_note; its content (friend -> amount, in 'I owe' vs 'owes me' sections) is modeled as static i-owe/they-owe facts gated by (note-read). Friend emails are modeled as static friend-email facts gated by (friends-listed), obtained with one venmo.search_friends call (no query); if the note already lists emails this call is redundant but harmless. The number of friends (2 I owe, 2 who owe me) is a placeholder matching the 11-call reference; instantiate one transaction per 'I owe' entry and one payment request per 'owes me' entry at runtime. Persons, amounts, the note, the description 'For Athens trip' and private=true are domain constants so supervisor-complete-task can state every goal condition in its precondition. Money I owe -> venmo.create_transaction (private, description 'For Athens trip'); money owed to me -> venmo.create_payment_request (private, same description). No answer is passed to complete_task.

plan: (venmo-create-transaction email-i-owe-1 amount-i-owe-1 venmo-token note-for-athens-trip private-true friend-i-owe-1 athens-trip-note)
(venmo-create-transaction email-i-owe-2 amount-i-owe-2 venmo-token note-for-athens-trip private-true friend-i-owe-2 athens-trip-note)
(venmo-create-payment-request email-owes-me-1 amount-owes-me-1 venmo-token note-for-athens-trip private-true friend-owes-me-1 athens-trip-note)
(venmo-create-payment-request email-owes-me-2 amount-owes-me-2 venmo-token note-for-athens-trip private-true friend-owes-me-2 athens-trip-note)
